scenes.title: Agamemnon Sleepless
scenes.summary: While the other chiefs sleep, Agamemnon lies awake, groaning as thick and fast as Zeus' lightning. When he looks toward Troy he marvels at the many fires and the sound of flutes and pipes; when he looks at his own army he tears out his hair. He resolves to go to Nestor for a plan, and puts on a tawny lion's skin and takes his spear.

scenes.title: The Brothers
scenes.summary: Menelaus cannot sleep either, fearing for the Argives who came to Troy for his sake. He puts on a leopard's skin and finds his brother arming by his ship. Agamemnon says they need shrewd counsel, since Zeus favors Hector, and sends Menelaus to call Ajax and Idomeneus while he goes to Nestor: he is to call out to each man by his father's name, honoring all, and not stand on his own rank.

scenes.title: Agamemnon Wakes Nestor
scenes.summary: Nestor lies in a soft bed by his hut with his armor beside him and the gleaming belt he wears to war. He raises himself on his elbow and challenges the visitor. Agamemnon tells him of his sleeplessness and fear, and asks him to come down to the sentries. Nestor answers that Zeus will not fulfill all Hector's hopes, proposes to wake Diomedes, Odysseus, swift Ajax and Meges, and blames Menelaus for sleeping; Agamemnon answers that Menelaus is already awake and out calling the chiefs.

scenes.title: Nestor Rouses the Chiefs
scenes.summary: Nestor puts on a double crimson cloak and takes his spear. He wakes Odysseus, who comes out of his hut and joins them, and then finds Diomedes asleep outside his hut on an ox-hide among his sleeping companions, their spears planted upright. He wakes him with his heel. Diomedes calls him a hard old man who never rests; Nestor agrees, but the need is great, since all stands on a razor's edge, and sends Diomedes to rouse swift Ajax and Meges.

scenes.title: Among the Sentries
scenes.summary: They find the leaders of the sentries awake and armed, watching like dogs that hear a wild beast coming through the woods. Nestor praises them. The kings cross the ditch with Meriones and Nestor's son and sit in a clear space free of corpses, where Hector turned back at nightfall.

scenes.title: Volunteers for the Night
scenes.summary: Nestor asks for a man to go among the Trojans and learn their plans, promising fame and a black ewe with her lamb from every chief. Diomedes volunteers and asks for a companion, since two see more than one. Many are willing; Agamemnon, fearing for Menelaus, tells Diomedes to choose the best and not the most kingly. Diomedes chooses Odysseus, whom Athena loves; Odysseus bids him not praise him too much, for the night is two parts gone.

scenes.title: The Arming and the Heron
scenes.summary: Thrasymedes gives Diomedes a sword, a shield and a leather skullcap; Meriones gives Odysseus a bow, a quiver, a sword and the boar's-tusk helmet, whose history runs from Autolycus' theft at Eleon through Amphidamas of Cythera and Molus to Meriones. Athena sends a heron on the right, heard but not seen. Odysseus prays to her for glory and a safe return; Diomedes recalls her help to his father Tydeus at Thebes and vows her a yearling heifer. They set out like two lions through the dead.

scenes.title: Hector Sends Dolon
scenes.summary: Hector too calls a council and offers a chariot and the two best horses at the Achaean ships to whoever will spy on the Achaeans. Dolon, son of the herald Eumedes, rich, ill-favored and swift, the only brother of five sisters, volunteers if Hector will swear to give him Achilles' horses and chariot. Hector swears by Zeus, an oath that would prove false. Dolon puts on a wolf's skin and a ferret-skin cap and sets out with a bow and a javelin.

scenes.title: The Capture of Dolon
scenes.summary: Odysseus sees him coming. The two lie down among the corpses and let him run past, then cut him off from his own lines, chasing him like two hounds after a fawn or a hare. Near the Achaean sentries Athena gives Diomedes strength; he casts his spear over Dolon's shoulder on purpose, and Dolon stops, teeth chattering, and offers a ransom of bronze, gold and iron.

scenes.title: Dolon Questioned
scenes.summary: Odysseus tells him to take heart and questions him. Dolon blames Hector's promise of Achilles' horses, which Odysseus says no mortal but Achilles can drive. He tells where Hector holds council, by the tomb of Ilus; that the Trojans keep watch at their own fires while the allies sleep; where each of the allies is camped; and that the Thracians lie apart, newly come, with King Rhesus and his horses, whiter than snow and swift as the winds, and his golden armor. He asks to be taken to the ships or left bound until they return.

scenes.title: The Death of Dolon
scenes.summary: Diomedes refuses: if they let him go he will come again to spy or to fight. As Dolon reaches for his chin to beg, Diomedes cuts through his neck. They strip him, and Odysseus holds up the cap, the wolf-skin, the bow and the spear to Athena, goddess of the spoil, and prays to her to guide them to the Thracians. He sets the spoils on a tamarisk and marks the place with reeds and branches.

scenes.title: The Killing of Rhesus
scenes.summary: They find the Thracians asleep in three rows with their armor and their horses, and Rhesus in the middle with his horses tied to his chariot. Athena breathes strength into Diomedes, who kills twelve men like a lion among flocks, while Odysseus drags the bodies aside so the horses will not shy. The thirteenth is Rhesus, over whose head Diomedes stands like an evil dream. Odysseus drives out the horses, striking them with his bow, and whistles; Diomedes wonders whether to take the chariot or kill more, until Athena tells him to go before another god wakes the Trojans. They ride off.

scenes.title: Apollo Rouses the Thracians
scenes.summary: Apollo, angry to see Athena with Diomedes, goes into the Trojan throng and wakes Hippocoon, Rhesus' cousin, who sees the empty place where the horses stood and the men gasping in their blood, and cries out to his friend. The Trojans rush together in uproar and gaze at what the two have done.

scenes.title: The Return
scenes.summary: At the place where they killed Dolon, Diomedes leaps down and hands the bloody spoils to Odysseus, and they ride on to the ships. Nestor hears the hooves and hopes that it is Odysseus and Diomedes. They ride in and are welcomed. Nestor asks whether a god gave them horses like the rays of the sun; Odysseus answers that a god could give even better, and tells of Rhesus, his twelve companions, and the thirteenth, Hector's spy.

scenes.title: Bath and Libation
scenes.summary: Odysseus drives the horses across the ditch, laughing, and they are tied at Diomedes' manger. Odysseus sets Dolon's spoils in the stern of a ship until an offering can be made to Athena. The two wash off their sweat in the sea, bathe in tubs, anoint themselves with oil, and sit down to eat, pouring wine to Athena.

days.label: Night of Day 25
days.note: The same night as Book 9, after the embassy has returned. Odysseus reckons that two of the night's three portions are gone when he and Diomedes set out (10.251–253), and they are back at the ships before dawn. Day 26 dawns at 11.1.
